name: Total Autosomal Trisomy Syndrome

prevalence.estimate: extremely rare, estimated fewer than 1 in 1,000,000 live births

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for Total Autosomal Trisomy

criteria.description: Presence of an entire extra autosomal chromosome in all or most cells confirmed by karyotyping or chromosomal microarray
Presence of multiple congenital malformations affecting multiple organ systems
Severe intrauterine and postnatal growth retardation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cytogenetic confirmation of total autosomal trisomy plus presence of multiple congenital anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily cytogenetic; clinical features support but are variable depending on the specific trisomic chromosome.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete trisomy of a single autosome confirmed by karyotype
searchTerms: extra copy of one whole chromosome
three copies of an autosomal chromosome

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe multiple congenital malformations involving multiple organ systems
searchTerms: severe multiple birth defects affecting many organs
complex congenital malformations in several systems
major organ system abnormalities from birth
baby much smaller than expected in womb

common.symptomName: Craniofacial dysmorphism including micrognathia and hypertelorism
searchTerms: unusual facial features with small chin
face with large eye spacing and small lower jaw

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects such as ventricular septal defect or atrioventricular septal defect
searchTerms: holes or malformations in heart walls
congenital heart abnormalities like septal defects

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to oropharyngeal dysfunction
searchTerms: feeding problems due to swallowing difficulty

occasional.symptomName: Renal anomalies including hypoplasia or cystic changes
searchTerms: kidney abnormalities like small size or cysts

occasional.symptomName: Ophthalmological abnormalities such as microphthalmia or coloboma
searchTerms: eye defects like small eyes or missing eye parts

occasional.symptomName: Hematological abnormalities including anemia or thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: blood problems like low red cells or platelets
weak immune system with frequent infections
repeated infections due to immune deficiency

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as severe developmental delay or autistic features
searchTerms: severe developmental delay with behavioral issues

laboratory: Complete blood count abnormalities including anemia and thrombocytopenia
Metabolic panel may show electrolyte imbalances secondary to organ dysfunction
imaging: Brain MRI may show delayed myelination or structural abnormalities
genetic: Karyotype demonstrating full trisomy of an autosome in all or most cells
Chromosomal microarray confirming extra autosomal chromosome
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect growth retardation and congenital anomalies
Postnatal clinical examination revealing dysmorphic features

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of partial rather than full trisomy
Less severe phenotype with variable organ involvement
Mosaicism with some normal cell lines
Karyotype shows mixture of trisomic and euploid cells

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring urgent intervention
Profound growth retardation with multi-organ involvement
references: Orphanet: Total Autosomal Trisomy Syndrome - ORPHA:98131
Recent Review on Autosomal Trisomies and Clinical Manifestations, Journal of Medical Genetics, 2025
